process-tools::night-auditor — GitHub MC.question: Should a GitHub MCP be installed/authenticated for this project, or should the night-auditor's PR/CI/push-verification section be explicitly waived?

options.label: Install GitHub MCP
options.desc: Add a Cowork or community GitHub MCP and authenticate it for the Process-Tools repo. Restores remote-PR/CI awareness; one-time install + auth surface.

options.label: Waive the PR/CI section
options.desc: Amend `roles/night-auditor.md` so the remote-PR/CI/push-verification step is explicitly out of scope; auditor relies on `git reflog` / `git ls-tree` for push verification only.

options.label: Defer until first miss
options.desc: Keep the local-only fallback. Revisit only when an actual PR-state question matters; risk is the gap bites silently the first time it does.

recommendation.rationale: Auditor has self-corrected on `git reflog` for two weeks with no signal loss; the install + auth cost outweighs the marginal value while no remote PRs are in flight.

process-tools::night-auditor — GitHub MC.unblocks: Closes the ~2-week-old NEEDS-INPUT entry and lets `roles/night-auditor.md` accurately describe its real scope.

process-tools::worker-11am — QUEUE is em.question: How should the chronically-empty automation queue be addressed — by answering the BPMN gate, by promoting PROPOSED items, or by accepting the empty-queue state?

options.label: Answer the BPMN gate
options.desc: Resolve the BPMN/Camunda P1 directly so the [in-progress] item closes and morning Workers see real work. Already partly addressed by the 2026-05-11 cowork-session — see eric-action item.

options.label: Promote PROPOSED items
options.desc: Approve one or more of the PROPOSED items (esp. the two P1s — commit-or-stash + `git read-tree HEAD` index refresh) so the planner can re-queue work.

options.label: Accept empty-queue state
options.desc: Stop treating empty-queue as a NEEDS-INPUT condition; let Workers exit clean when nothing is pickable. Simplest, but loses the daily nag that surfaces backlog stagnation.

recommendation.rationale: Backlog has 11+ items; the two P1s are blocking-adjacent and would compound across every future morning chain. Promoting them is one evening-review pass with high leverage.

process-tools::worker-11am — QUEUE is em.unblocks: Lets morning Worker shifts pick up actual work instead of writing daily empty-queue NEEDS-INPUT entries; clears 2 P1 PROPOSED items in the same pass.

process-tools::worker-12pm — BPMN/Camund.question: How should the BPMN/Camunda P1's unattended-approval gap be bridged — attended Worker session, Eric runs the validation, or accept structural pins as sufficient?

options.label: Attended Worker session (B1)
options.desc: Eric stays present to click `request_access` dialogs while a Worker drives Camunda Modeler + Chrome via computer-use. Closest to the original automation framing; costs ~1 attended slot.

options.label: Eric runs it himself (B2)
options.desc: Eric does the ~15-minute section-2 checklist manually; queue item becomes an `[eric-action]` row. No automation changes; trades worker time for human time.

options.label: Accept pins, drop GUI step (B3)
options.desc: Treat the structural validator (24/24) + unittest pins (40/40) as sufficient for v1.0; drop `[in-progress]`, defer GUI gate. Lowest cost, weakest assurance.

recommendation.rationale: Already adopted in the 2026-05-11 cowork-session; the live form is the `[eric-action / 2026-05-11]` NEEDS-INPUT row. One 15-minute pass closes the 2-week-old P1.

process-tools::worker-12pm — BPMN/Camund.unblocks: QUEUE 2.5 P1 closes; CLAUDE.md task-specific waiver self-sunsets; structural-validator-extension queue items unblock.

process-tools::researcher — What bounded.question: Which bounded research question should the next 04:00 researcher slot prioritize?

options.desc: Post-fix retro on the 2026-05-06 `.git/index` corruption mechanism. Tunes how seriously to treat future trailer-SHA1 mismatch flags. Gated on the lock clearing.

options.label: R2 — index.lock holder forensics
options.desc: Identify which Windows-side process took the lock at 2026-04-29 17:10 UTC and never released. Requires Windows-side access (Process Monitor, Event Viewer, AV logs).

options.label: R3 — Pre-Phase-4 readiness audit
options.desc: Sweep the four sub-tools for CHANGELOG depth, version-bump consistency, PyInstaller spec gaps, and offline-target smoke-test footprint before Phase 4 (bundle/cut/tag) opens.

options.desc: Mark `[answered] no question; skip` so tomorrow's 04:00 researcher idle-exits cleanly without inventing a question.

recommendation.rationale: De-risks the v1.0 cut, doable from the Linux audit env (no Windows-side access needed), and surfaces Phase-4 gaps before a Worker hits them mid-shift.
